Estimate which month the snapshot describes. Use only the figures supplied plus your general knowledge of economic history.

text:
The fed funds rate is 4.33% after 100bp of cuts over 12 months, which points to early 2025 (cuts in Sep, Nov and Dec 2024 brought the range to 4.25-4.50%). Unemployment of 4.1% fits that period, and the 10-year yield at 4.52% fits January or February 2025.

Other figures match January 2025. Headline CPI of 2.9% YoY was the January 2025 reading, and core CPI of 3.25% is probably a rounded figure close to 3.2%. Gold up 37% over 12 months fits, and so does the strong dollar. US equity returned 24% over 12 months with a 1.3% drawdown, so equities were near their high, as in January 2025. Developed ex-US rose 4.8% in the month, which also fits January.

Some details do not fit February. The VIX at 15.84 is lower than the roughly 16 seen at the end of January, and it fell 7.3 points over 3 months, from about 23 in October or November. The policy rate's 3-month change of -0.50 matches cuts in November and December, consistent with a January snapshot.

Gold up 7.5% in the month fits February better, since it was up about 6.5% in January and 2% in February. The 1-month US equity return of 2.3% fits January (about 2.8%), while February was about -1%. The 10-year yield ended January at 4.54%, and 4.52% fits that. Payrolls averaged 170k, which fits the January data. Overall, January 2025 is the best match.
